title: Why onions make you cry (and how to stop it instantly) #shorts
description:
Learn why cutting onions triggers tears and a quick way to avoid the sting. We explain the chemistry and give an instant tip you can try right now.

Narration is a synthetic voice. Script and visuals are produced with AI tools and checked by automated quality gates.

scenes.say: Why onions make you cry (and how to stop it instantly)
When you slice an onion, it releases a volatile gas that irritates your eyes.
The gas is syn‑propanethial‑S‑oxide, produced when the enzyme alliinase meets sulfur compounds.
The gas diffuses into the air and reaches your eyes in seconds.
In your tears it reacts with water, forming a tiny amount of sulfuric‑like acid that stings nerve endings.
Cool the onion first to chilling it for about ten minutes slows the enzyme, so far less gas is made.
Another fast fix: cut the onion near a running tap or under a fan to blow the gas away.
Now you can dice without tears. Follow for more ten‑second science.
